Written comments will be accepted via email at Cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. They will be shared with

records that will be made available for public viewing.

modification or accommodation to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk's Office at
(909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

Agenda Report
DATE:  June 11, 2025

TO:  Public Finance Authority (EIFD)

FROM:  Ken Domer, Executive Director

SUBJECT:  PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION APPROVING
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2024-25 ANNUAL REPORT FOR THE PUBLIC
  FINANCING AUTHORITY OF THE LA VERNE ENHANCED
  INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING DISTRICT

SUMMARY

In accordance with Government Code Section 53398.66(j)(2) and (3), PFA Resolution
25-01 and the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Annual Report for the Public Financing Authority
(PFA) of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD) are presented for
consideration at tonight’s Public Hearing. The annual report is required to include the
financial information from the previous fiscal year. As a result of the way in which projects
are being paid for through a City issued bond rather than the EIFD, this agenda report
also provides information on those revenues expenditures.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended the PFA Board conduct a public hearing on the Annual Report, taking
any written or verbal testimony, and then adopt PFA Resolution No. 25-01 adopting the
Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Annual Report of the City of La Verne Public Financing Authority
for the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District.

DISCUSSION

Background
In 2017, the City created an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District. The purpose of
the district was to fund over $33 million in City infrastructure projects anticipated to
support the A Line (formerly Gold Line) light rail transit riders as well as facilitate the
Transit Oriented Development expected to occur with the addition of the rail service. An
EIFD allows the City to fund these improvement projects through Tax Increment
Financing (TIF). The EIFD receives its revenue by the incremental property tax that is
generated within the designated area as development occurs and property taxes
increase.

Annual Report
State law requires that an Annual Report be approved for any Enhanced Infrastructure
Financing District (EIFD) through a public hearing process before the Public Finance
Authority (PFA) of the EIFD.
 2024-2025 Annal Report of the City of La Verne - Public Financing Authority for the EIFD
June 11, 2025
Page 2

On May 8, 2025, the draft Annual Report was mailed to all property owners within the
EIFD area and posted to the City’s website on the dedicated EIFD page
(www.cityoflaverne.org/eifd) as required by law. The report is to include a list of projects
that were undertaken in the year funded by the EIFD, the property tax increment collected,
expenses, and projected property tax increment for the coming year. The report also is
required to state the date and time of the public hearing in accordance with state law.
There have been no comments received to date related to the mailing or website posting.

It is recommended the Board hold the required Public Hearing regarding the Annual
Report, and after any public comments, adopt the Resolution approving the report.

FISCAL ANALYSIS

EIFD FY 2024-2025 Annual Report
The following is the fiscal information related to the EIFD included in the Annual Report:

Revenues and Expenses for 2024-2025:
  Property Tax Increment: EIFD Fund Balance on 7/1/2024:  $ 267,446.00
  Projected 2024-2025 Revenue:  $ 100,676.00
  Projected Fund Balance on 6/30/2025:  $ 343,792.00

  Expenses: $24,330

EIFD Projects and City Bonds
By its nature, an EIFD needs time to create a sustained revenue stream to support the
projects it is expected to fund. To enable the funding of these infrastructure projects in
advance of the EIFD’s increased revenues, the City opted to issue bonds in June 2022.
The debt payments were to be funded with La Verne’s Prop C Funds with the EIFD
ultimately obligated to reimburse the City at a future date once the District is fiscally
sustainable. The Bond Issuance structure is detailed in the June 6, 2022, La Verne City
Council Agenda Report, included as an attachment.

The 2022 bond issuance amount was $3,600,000. The project prioritized for this bond
funding was the E & Second Street Improvements Project designed to provide
connectivity and pedestrian improvements between the future light rail station and Old
Town La Verne. Since the costs of this completed project have been paid by the Bond
rather than the PFA, these expenses are not shown in the Annual Report for the EIFD.
However, it is important to document these expenses for the PFA’s benefit which is why
the costs are included in the fiscal impact.

The attached Public Financing Authority Statement from May 2024 through April 2025
reflects bond expenses for the Pedestrian Bridge project as $635,910, with an additional
$1,320,000 committed for future Pedestrian Bridge expenses. The Statement reflects a
balance of $200,070 for future projects identified in the EIFD’s Infrastructure Financing

Plan. It also notes the annual payment of the 20-year debt service schedule which was
$257,457.50 paid for by the City’s Prop C funds.

Based on the EIFD’s current Fund Balance and projected revenues at this time, its ability
to reimburse the City for the annual debt service payments will be several years into the
future.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
None.

LEGAL REVIEW
This report was approved by the City Attorney.

Report Prepared By:
Debra Fritz, Deputy City Clerk
   2024-2025
  Annual Report of the City of La Verne
  Public Financing Authority for the
  Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
This Annual Report is issued in accordance with the requirements of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District Law
(53398.66.). The Authority has entered into a reimbursement agreement with the City in order to fund street
improvements on E and 2nd Streets. The City has issued a bond in 2022 with the lease payments for such bond from the
City’s Proposition C Fund until such time the EIFD is in the financial position to begin repaying the debt. The bond funded
the now completed E and 2nd Street Improvement Project. Any remaining funds from the initial bond are planned as a
contribution to the construction of the proposed Arrow Highway Multimodal (Pedestrian and Bicycle) Bridge. Design
work is close to completion on the Bridge, but the costs associated with this project are being paid by the San Gabriel
Valley Council of Government (SGVCOG) using Measure M dollars and the City’s Proposition C fund. Thus, there are no
direct fiscal costs for these projects to the District in this reporting period. The minor expenses in this reporting period
are for the general administration of the District.
  A. Projects Undertaken in Fiscal Year 2024-2025:
  Pedestrian Bridge Design – Agreement with San Gabrel Valley Council of Governments for project
  management (with costs paid for by the City’s 2022 bond).

  B. Revenues and Expenses for 2024-2025 (estimated):
  Property Tax Increment and Bond Activity:
  Fund Balance on 7/1/2024:  $267,143
  Projected 2024-2025 Revenue:  $97,676
  Projected Fund Balance on 6/30/2025: $359,319
  Expenses: $5,500
  C. Amount of Property Tax Increment Projected to be Received for Fiscal Year 2025-2026: $100,600

  D. Revenues expended for Housing:
  None to date.

  E. Assessment of completion of Projects in Fiscal Year 2024-2025: No projects expected to be completed.
  F. In progress:
  Pedestrian Bridge Design – Design essentially complete with funding from SGVCOG – Measure M, City’s
  Proposition C Fund, EIFD Bond, and federal appropriations.
  Funding from City Bond – Lease payments currently made by City’s Proposition C. EIFD will have responsibility to
  reimburse for these expenses once EIFD Fund Balance can support the payments.
  G. Amount of Revenue expended to assist private businesses: None to date.

A public hearing on this annual report will be held before the Public Financing Authority on Wednesday, June 11,
2025, at 9:00 a.m. The meeting will be held at La Verne City Hall at 3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750. The agenda will
be posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting at City Hall and at www.cityoflaverne.org. This report is also available
on the dedicated EIFD page at www.cityoflaverne.org/EIFD.

Should you have any questions regarding this report, please email cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org or call 909-596-8726.
